property_summary: After any single successful external call to Put by any caller with any nonzero ETH value, the contract's nonReentrant_ modifier in the reference resets locked_ so that a subsequent Put call by the same caller still succeeds (does not revert); the mutant removes resetting locked_ causing subsequent Put calls to always revert once any Put has been called, breaking this property for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero value, calling Put succeeds every time on the reference (nonReentrant_ is reset after call), whereas the mutant that never resets locked_ will cause a subsequent Put call to revert (fail) for some inputs (e.g., when the same caller calls Put twice with value>0).

For any caller and any nonzero ether value, after one successful Put call the reference contract remains usable by other callers (they can still call Put successfully), while the mutant that permanently leaves locked_ = true will block subsequent Put calls from any caller (so some other caller's Put will fail).

For any two distinct callers and any nonzero deposit amounts, the reference contract allows both callers to successfully call Put (the reentrancy lock is cleared after each call), whereas the mutant that never clears the lock will make the second caller's Put revert for some inputs (when the first call sets locked_ permanently).

For any caller and any nonzero ETH value, calling Put twice in succession (first call succeeds) leaves the contract unlocked in the reference so the second Put also succeeds; the mutant that never clears the reentrancy lock makes the second Put revert for some inputs (the second call fails).

For any caller and any provided _unlockTime and msg.value, after calling Put the contract's Acc(msg.sender).unlockTime is at least the current block.timestamp (i.e., Put never sets unlockTime in the past); the mutant that assigns unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it in the past and thus violates this rule for some inputs.

For any caller, after calling Put(_unlockTime) with any value and any payment, the contract's Acc(caller).unlockTime is never less than the block.timestamp (Put sets unlockTime = max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)); the mutant that assigns unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it in the past and thus violates this property for some inputs.

For any caller, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the stored Acc(caller).unlockTime is >= the block.timestamp at the time of the call (reference enforces max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)); the mutant that assigns unlockTime = _unlockTime can leave it < block.timestamp for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller and any _unlockTime and payment, after calling Put the stored Acc(caller).unlockTime is never less than the block.timestamp at the time of the call; the mutant that assigns unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it less than block.timestamp for some inputs.

After calling Put(_unlockTime) from any caller with any payment, the reference contract ensures the stored Acc(caller).unlockTime is >= block.timestamp (it uses max), while the mutant which assigns unlockTime = _unlockTime can produce a stored unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, causing the property to fail.

For any caller and any deposit value, after calling Put(...) the caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance increases by exactly the sent msg.value (so stored balance >= msg.value and equals previous balance + msg.value); the mutant that omits updating acc.balance breaks this (for some inputs the stored balance does not increase while the contract still accepted funds).

After any caller successfully calls Put with some nonzero msg.value, the contract's stored Acc[caller].balance is at least the sent value (i.e., deposits are recorded); the mutant that removes updating acc.balance accepts ETH but does not increase the stored balance, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposit amount, after calling Put(...) the contract's on-chain ETH balance increases by the same msg.value (reference: stored Acc may track balance but buggy mutant still accepts ETH into contract while not updating Acc; the invariant: address(c).balance increases by msg.value always holds in reference and also in mutant — so instead we assert that after Put, the stored Acc[caller].unlockTime equals the max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp) which the reference sets and the mutant also sets; to distinguish we instead assert that after Put with zero msg.value the caller's Acc[caller].balance is unchanged (i.e., depositing 0 does not change stored balance) — BUT the bug removes updating balance on any deposit, so for some positive deposit inputs the mutant will leave stored balance unchanged; therefore we use a two-step sequence: first Put with some initial deposit to set balance, then Put again with additional deposit and check that Acc balance increased by that additional amount — reference always increases stored Acc balance by msg.value, mutant does not, so assertion fails on mutant for many inputs.

For any address and any two deposits (nonzero first to establish a nonzero starting recorded balance), after making an initial Put with amount a and then a second Put with amount b, the stored Acc[address].balance increases by exactly b (i.e., final recorded balance = initial recorded balance + b); the mutant that removes updating acc.balance on Put will break this for some inputs where b>0.

For any caller, performing a Put with a positive msg.value increases that caller's recorded Acc balance (final Acc[msg.sender].balance >= prior Acc[msg.sender].balance + msg.value); the mutant that omits updating acc.balance will violate this after a positive deposit.

After a successful Put followed by a successful Collect that withdraws some funds, the account balance for the caller becomes decreased by the withdrawn amount (i.e. Collect succeeds exactly once and reduces balance).

property_summary: A single call to Collect(...) by this test account that meets preconditions should not revert (i.e., Collect succeeds) on the original contract.

If the caller has >= MinSum balance and enough unlocked funds, a single Collect call that would otherwise be allowed on the original contract does not revert (i.e., Collect can succeed at least once).

If a single call to Collect from this tester reverts, then it must be because the caller's balance is below MinSum or below the requested amount or the unlockTime has not passed (i.e., Collect should only revert when preconditions about balance/time fail).
If Collect reverted then this test's account balance did not increase due to the call (i.e., reverts prevent Ether being sent to the caller).

After any successful Collect call by an address with sufficient balance and expired unlockTime, the reference contract resets its reentrancy lock allowing subsequent Collect calls to succeed (or at least not be permanently blocked), whereas the mutant that never clears the lock leaves the contract permanently locked so a later Collect call from the same caller will revert; thus reference always allows a second Collect to attempt success while mutant makes the second call revert for some inputs.

For any caller, if they successfully call Collect once (so it does not revert), then a second Collect call with the same caller and same conditions will also be allowed to execute (not permanently blocked by a stuck reentrancy lock) — the mutant that never clears locked_ makes the second Collect call revert for some inputs.

For any caller and admissible inputs, if the caller successfully calls Collect(...) once (the call returns without revert), then a second identical Collect(...) call from the same caller immediately afterwards will also succeed on the reference contract; the mutant that never clears the reentrancy lock causes the second call to revert for some inputs.

For any caller that performs a successful Collect(amount) (i.e., the call returns), the reference contract leaves locked_ cleared so that a subsequent independent call to Put by the same caller (payable) still succeeds and increases the caller's recorded balance; the mutant that never clears locked_ leaves the contract locked after Collect causing a later Put to revert (or not update balance) for some inputs.

For any caller and admissible amounts: if the caller has sufficient balance and unlockTime passed and a first Collect(...) call succeeds, then immediately attempting a second Collect(...) with the same caller and same amount will also succeed on the correct contract (the reentrancy lock is cleared), whereas the mutant that never clears the lock makes that second call revert for some inputs.
